name: Singapore — December 2025
change_summary: The law as it stood in December 2025: the 2025 CPF tables — above-55-to-60 at 32.5% (15.5% employer, 17% employee), above-60-to-65 at 23.5% (12% / 11.5%), the ordinary-wage ceiling $7,400 — with the same SDL, self-help-group, work and leave rows as the 1 January 2026 version, which succeeds it with the 2026 senior-worker step and the $8,000 ceiling.

limits.authority: Employment Act 1968 s.38(1): not more than 44 hours of work in one week; s.38(4) pays the hours beyond at not less than one and a half times the hourly basic rate
EA s.38(5) as MOM reads it: the 72 hours a month include work on a rest day or public holiday beyond the normal daily hours; reported beside the regulated count the ladder funnels on.

work_rules.authority: Employment Act 1968 Part 4. s.38(4) — work beyond normal hours is paid at not less than one and a half times the hourly basic rate of pay (in this form since 1 March 1996, Act 36 of 1995). s.38(1) not more than 44 hours in one week, carried by the `weekly_normal` limit payroll reads: normal-day hours past the 44th in a Monday-to-Sunday week are overtime of the day they fall on. s.38(5) 72 overtime hours a month; s.38(8) 12 hours in any one day. s.38(1)(a) a break after more than 6 consecutive hours; s.38(1)(c) at least 45 minutes in the aggregate where work requiring continual attendance runs 8 consecutive hours. s.36 one rest day a week, and where a monthly roster is drawn up not more than 12 days between two rest days. s.37(3) rest-day pay at the employer's request; s.37(3)(c)(ii) pays the hours beyond the normal day "for each hour or part thereof", so the rest-day OT-1.5X band rounds its slice up to the hour. s.88 a public holiday falling on a rest day is observed on the next working day. s.35 and the First Schedule: Part 4 applies to a workman earning a basic monthly salary of not more than SGD 4,500 and to a non-workman (other than a manager or executive) earning not more than SGD 2,600. `overtime_when` applies both ceilings: `terms.statutory_work_category == "NON_MANUAL"` is the non-workman (SGD 2,600); every other category is a workman (SGD 4,500). s.88(4) an extra day's salary at the basic rate of pay for work on a public holiday. Rates: Fourth Schedule, hourly basic rate = 12 × monthly basic ÷ (52 × 44), carried by `rate_week_hours` (44 for every full-time monthly-rated employee, whatever the contract's week) over `ordinary_divisor_days`; Third Schedule item 2, basic rate for one day = 12 × monthly basic ÷ (52 × days required to work in a week), which the day-wage bands price directly from `person.terms` because one divisor cannot yield both figures for a week under 44 hours. s.38(1) normal day: 9 hours on a week of five days or fewer, else 8 (`normal_hours`; a longer shift is a normal day plus overtime). s.37(2): rest-day work at the employee’s request pays half a day up to half the normal hours and one day beyond (`requested_by`), against s.37(3)’s one and two at the employer’s. s.88(4A)/MOM: a public holiday that falls on a non-working day (neither a working day nor the rest day) is a day off in lieu or an extra day’s salary; the `PH-NON-WORKING-DAY` band prices the day’s salary on such a day read and found empty (a `work_days` row with no work), taking no hours. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): EA Third Schedule: the basic rate for a day is the daily rate for a daily-rated employee, the hourly rate × the hours of the normal day for an hourly-rated one, and 12 × monthly ÷ (52 × days a week) for a monthly-rated one (`person.terms.pay_frequency` in the day-wage bands). Applied 2026-09-19 (2): EA s.38(1)(a): work that must be carried on continuously may run eight consecutive hours with a break of at least 45 minutes for a meal — the break is owed at eight (`>= 8.0`), not only beyond it. Applied 2026-09-23 (SG audit): s.35 measures "a salary not exceeding $2,600 [$4,500] a month", so the Part 4 bands turn a daily, hourly or weekly rate into its month (daily × 52 × days a week ÷ 12; hourly × weekly hours × 52 ÷ 12; weekly × 52 ÷ 12) before comparing it; the raw rate put every daily- or hourly-rated employee inside Part 4. s.88 is Part 10 of the Employment Act and reaches no employee outside it: the two public-holiday bands exclude `NON_EA`. s.88(1)(c) pays a holiday on a non-working day at the gross rate of pay (s.2: allowances included, other than travelling, food or housing): the `PH-NON-WORKING-DAY` band prices a monthly-rated employee on `person.terms.monthly_wage` — basic plus the contract's fixed allowances, which can only exceed the s.2 gross rate where a travelling, food or housing allowance is fixed on the contract. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): the Part 4 salary test reads `person.terms.monthly_basic` (a daily, hourly or weekly rate taken to its month on the ordinary divisor, 52 × days ÷ 12), and the Third Schedule day reads `person.terms.ordinary_day` (12 × monthly ÷ (52 × days); a weekly wage is now its week over the days, not read as a month). s.2 “gross rate of pay” excludes travelling, food and housing allowances: `PH-NON-WORKING-DAY` prices `person.terms.gross_monthly`, net of the allowance codes in `gross_excluded_allowances` (the company’s own codes; none are seeded). s.88(1)(c) and s.88(4A): the entity fact `public_holiday_compensation` = TIME_OFF records the employer’s election of a day off instead of pay — the non-working-day band stops, and the extra day’s salary for holiday work stops for an employee outside Part 4 who is not a workman (non-workman above $2,600 or a manager); the Part 4 hours beyond the normal day stay paid.

encashment.day_amount: terms.fixed_allowances * 12.0 / (52.0 * terms.working_days_per_week) + (terms.pay_frequency == "DAILY" ? terms.basic_salary : terms.pay_frequency == "HOURLY" ? terms.basic_salary * terms.ordinary_hours_per_week / terms.working_days_per_week : terms.pay_frequency == "WEEKLY" ? terms.basic_salary / terms.working_days_per_week : terms.basic_salary * 12.0 / (52.0 * terms.working_days_per_week))
encashment.authority: Employment Act s.2 gross rate; MOM Monthly and daily salary; MOM Termination with notice: last drawn gross salary. Excludes overtime, bonuses, reimbursements, productivity incentives, travel, food and housing allowances. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5): WEEKLY, DAILY and HOURLY. EmA 1968 s.2: “gross rate of pay” is the money including allowances an employee is entitled to “for working for a period of time, that is, for one hour, one day, one week, one month”, less overtime, bonus/AWS, reimbursements, productivity incentives and travelling, food or housing allowances. Third Schedule item 2 (s.107A) prices a monthly-rated day at 12 × monthly gross ÷ (52 × days required a week); a daily rate is the day itself, an hourly rate is the day’s contractual normal hours (weekly hours ÷ days a week), a weekly rate is the week over the days required in it (item 2 on 12 months = 52 weeks), and a monthly contract allowance adds its item 2 day share. Piece rates (item 1: the 14 days before, over the days actually worked) have no pay frequency here.

deduction_ceiling.authority: Employment Act 1968 s.32(1): all deductions in a salary period other than under s.27(1)(a) (absence), (f) (advances, loans, overpayments) and (j) (co-operative society) may not exceed 50% of the salary payable for that period — CPF contributions (s.27(1)(h)) count; s.32(2): the last salary on termination or completion of the contract is outside the limit. Not applied: the per-instalment quarter caps of s.31(3) and (5).

final_pay_deadlines.authority: Employment Act 1968 s.23(2): an employee who resigns without the notice s.10 requires, or before it expires, is paid within 7 days; one who served it is paid on the last day (s.23(1), the default rule)

tax_clearance.authority: Income Tax Act 1947 s.68(5)-(7); IRAS tax clearance withholds all monies until the Clearance Directive. IRAS (Tax Clearance for Foreign & SPR Employees): a permanent resident who is not leaving Singapore permanently gives a Letter of Undertaking and no IR21 is filed, so a permanent resident is held only when recorded as leaving.

sources.instructions:
Sources are the primary instrument first — the statute or regulation in the national law database, the gazette, or the table the authority itself publishes — one page per fact the version seals, never a news article or a commentary. A historical version lists the instruments in force on its own effective date. Where the primary host refuses the reader (sso.agc.gov.sg, officialgazette.gov.ph, peraturan.bpk.go.id, kwsp.gov.my, hrdcorp.gov.my answer 403 to Norbital-Public-Page-Reader) the authority’s own published table is listed instead, or the Wayback Machine’s dated copy of the authority’s own page or PDF (web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<url>) — never a host the reader cannot open.
sso.agc.gov.sg — Singapore Statutes Online: every Act and subsidiary legislation, HTML. /Act/EmA1968 is the Employment Act; add ?ProvIds=P14- for Part 4 (ss.35–53: rest days, hours, overtime), ?ProvIds=P19- for Part 9 (sick leave), ?ProvIds=P110- for Part 10 (public holidays); a #pr37- fragment lands on one section. /Act/CPFA1953 is the CPF Act, /Act/CDCSA2001 the Child Development Co-Savings Act.
cpf.gov.sg — CPF Board. /employer/employer-obligations/how-much-cpf-contributions-to-pay links the rate tables; the tables are PDFs under /content/dam/web/employer/employer-obligations/documents/ (CPFcontributionratesfrom1Jan2026.pdf, jan2027cpfcontributionrates.pdf; 0.2 MB, text) with Tables 1–5 by citizenship year and age. /employer/infohub/news/cpf-related-announcements/new-contribution-rates announces a step. /employer/employer-obligations/skills-development-levy is SDL; /employer/employer-obligations/contributions-to-self-help-groups the CDAC/ECF/MBMF/SINDA tables.
mom.gov.sg — /employment-practices/hours-of-work-overtime-and-rest-days (44 h, 1.5×, 72 h, $4,500/$2,600), /employment-practices/public-holidays (the gazetted list per year), /employment-practices/leave/<scheme>, /employment-practices/salary/monthly-and-daily-salary.
profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg — /schemes/<maternity-leave|paternity-leave|shared-parental-leave|childcare-leave|unpaid-infant-care-leave|adoption-leave>: the entitlement, its commencement date and eligibility.
muis.gov.sg — the MBMF contribution table by wage tier.

Finding changes (read these before comparing, every run):
1) Read https://sso.agc.gov.sg/What's-New/New-Legislation/RSS (newest first). Flag titles containing Central Provident Fund, Employment, Retirement, Child Development Co-Savings, Skills Development Levy, Holidays, Income Tax (rates/reliefs/Bills), Foreign Manpower (Levy), Workplace Fairness; open the linked SL-Supp/Acts-Supp page and read the commencement clause. 2) For a sealed Act, read https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/<CODE>?ViewType=Rss — any provision with a ValidDate after the version's seal date is a candidate. A provision as at a date: /Act/<CODE>?ValidDate=YYYYMMDD&ProvIds=Sc1- (CPF First Schedule). Title search: /Search/Content?Phrase=<words>&In=InForce_Act_SL&Within=title. 3) CPF: cpf-related-announcements and news-releases pages, then the rate page and its PDF tables. 4) MOM: press-releases?category=Employment+practices (&page=N); public-holidays page carries next year's list. 5) IRAS newsroom. SSO answers 403 to non-browser UAs — use the real browser. Discovery only: https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/singapore/individual/significant-developments — then open the official instrument before citing.

exit_facts.label: Resigned with due notice
exit_facts.description: The employee resigned after giving the notice s.10 requires (or paid salary in lieu under s.11); the total salary is then due on the day the contract ends (Employment Act 1968 s.23(1)), not within 7 days (s.23(2)).

exit_facts.label: Leaving Singapore permanently
exit_facts.description: A Singapore permanent resident leaving Singapore permanently: the employer seeks tax clearance (Form IR21) and withholds all monies (Income Tax Act 1947 s.68(7)). A permanent resident who is staying gives a Letter of Undertaking instead, and no IR21 is filed.

exit_facts.label: Dismissed for misconduct
exit_facts.description: Dismissed on grounds of misconduct after due inquiry (Employment Act 1968 s.14(1)); s.88A(8) then withholds the pay for untaken annual leave.

obligations.description: Submit and pay the month's CPF contributions (employer and employee shares) for every Singapore Citizen and SPR employee, with the SDL and self-help-group deductions, through the employer's CPF Submission Number; apply to CPF Board for a refund of contributions paid in excess of the Additional Wage ceiling (the payslip never credits it back).
obligations.trigger: Wages payable for a calendar month to a Citizen or SPR employee
obligations.timing: By the 14th of the following month (the next working day if the 14th is a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday); late payment interest 1.5% a month from the day after the due date, minimum $5.
obligations.owner: Finance / CPF submission advice and payment receipt
obligations.authority: Central Provident Fund Act 1953; CPF Board, When is the due date for CPF contributions (https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/when-is-the-due-date-for-cpf-contributions) and How does CPF Board calculate interest on late payment (https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/how-does-cpf-board-calculate-interest-on-late-payment).

obligations.description: Pay the Skills Development Levy for every employee working in Singapore, foreign employees included; the per-employee levies are summed and the total rounded down to the nearest dollar. An employer with only foreign employees pays SWDA directly.
obligations.trigger: Remuneration payable for a calendar month to any employee
obligations.timing: With the month's CPF contributions, by the 14th of the following month.
obligations.owner: Finance / CPF submission advice (SDL line) or SWDA receipt
obligations.authority: Skills Development Levy Act 1979; CPF Board, Skills Development Levy (https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/skills-development-levy). The engine prices each employee's levy; the whole-dollar rounding of the total and the payment are outside it.

obligations.description: Deduct the self-help-group contribution (CDAC, ECF, MBMF, SINDA) from the wages of each employee the fund reaches and remit it with CPF; apply a fund's written opt-out or changed-amount instruction from its effective date and keep it.
obligations.trigger: Wages payable for a calendar month to an employee within a fund
obligations.timing: With the month's CPF contributions, by the 14th of the following month.
obligations.owner: Payroll / fund instruction on file and CPF submission advice
obligations.authority: CPF Board, Contributions to self-help groups (https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/contributions-to-self-help-groups). The engine prices the deduction and reads the recorded instruction; obtaining the instruction and remitting are outside it.

obligations.description: Pay the monthly foreign worker levy for every Work Permit and S Pass holder; the payroll engine does not price it.
obligations.trigger: A Work Permit or S Pass is in force during the month
obligations.timing: By the 17th of the following month (the next working day if it falls on a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday), normally by GIRO; a late payment penalty accrues, and missing two consecutive months revokes the employer's existing Work Permits and S Passes the following month.
obligations.owner: Finance / MOM levy statement and GIRO receipt
obligations.authority: Employment of Foreign Manpower Act 1990 and the levy order made under it; MOM, Paying the foreign worker levy (https://www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/work-permit-for-foreign-worker/foreign-worker-levy/paying-the-levy).

obligations.description: Employ a foreign employee only while a valid work pass is in force and cancel the pass when the employment ends; count a local employee towards the Work Permit / S Pass quota only when paid at least the Local Qualifying Salary ($1,800 a month full-time; $10.50 an hour part-time under 35 hours a week).
obligations.trigger: Hiring, pass renewal or cessation of a foreign employee; each quota computation
obligations.timing: Before the foreign employee starts work; cancellation when the employment ends; the LQS on every month counted for quota.
obligations.owner: HR / work-pass records and quota computation
obligations.authority: Employment of Foreign Manpower Act 1990 s.5(1); MOM, Local Qualifying Salary (https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/progressive-wage-model/local-qualifying-salary).

obligations.description: Give each employee a written record of the key employment terms (salary, salary period, hours, leave, deductions, and the other prescribed terms).
obligations.trigger: An employee who entered a contract on or after 1 April 2016 and is employed for 14 days or more
obligations.timing: Not later than 14 days after the day the employee starts employment.
obligations.owner: HR / issued KET record
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1968 s.95A(2) (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968).

obligations.description: Give an itemised pay slip with the prescribed items (basic salary, allowances, overtime hours and pay, other additional payments, deductions including CPF, net salary, dates) for all salary paid for each salary period, and for every sum paid on dismissal or resignation.
obligations.trigger: Every salary payment, and every payment under EA s.22 or s.23
obligations.timing: Together with the payment, or within 3 working days after it.
obligations.owner: Payroll / issued pay slips (hard copy or electronic)
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1968 s.96 (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968); MOM, Itemised pay slips (https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/salary/itemised-payslips). The engine produces the payslip content; issuing it is outside it.

obligations.description: Keep complete and accurate employee records (particulars, start and leaving dates, working hours, public holidays and leave taken) and salary records (basic salary, allowances, additional payments, deductions, overtime hours and pay, net salary, payment dates), accessible to the employee or former employee.
obligations.trigger: Every employee and former employee covered by the Employment Act
obligations.timing: Current employees: the latest two years; former employees: the last two years, kept for one year after the employee leaves.
obligations.owner: HR and Payroll / record store
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1968 s.95 (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968); MOM, Employment records (https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/employment-records).

obligations.description: Fix a salary period of not more than one month and pay salary for it on time; pay overtime separately if needed.
obligations.trigger: The close of each salary period
obligations.timing: Salary before the expiry of the 7th day after the last day of the salary period; additional payments for overtime not later than 14 days after the last day of the salary period in which the work was done.
obligations.owner: Payroll / payment records
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1968 ss.20, 21(1)–(2) (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968).

obligations.description: Pay the total salary and every sum due on termination.
obligations.trigger: Employment ends
obligations.timing: Contract completed or employee terminates with due notice or under s.11: on the last day (s.21(3), s.23(1)); dismissal: on the day of dismissal or, if not possible, within 3 days thereafter, not being a rest day or public holiday (s.22); employee leaves without notice or before notice expires: before the expiry of the 7th day after termination (s.23(2)). Subject to income-tax clearance under s.24.
obligations.owner: Payroll / payment receipt and termination record
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1968 ss.21(3), 22, 23 (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968). The engine warns when a run's pay date passes the version's `payroll.final_pay_deadlines`; those rows cannot yet tell a resignation or retrenchment with notice served (due on the last day) from one without.

obligations.description: Make only deductions the Act authorises (absence, damage or loss, consented accommodation or amenities, advances and overpayments, CPF, court or Comptroller orders, consented others) and keep the total of those subject to the limit within 50% of the salary for the period; a written consent may be withdrawn before the deduction.
obligations.trigger: Any deduction from salary
obligations.timing: Each salary period; the 50% limit does not apply to the last salary on termination.
obligations.owner: Payroll / deduction authorities and consents
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1968 ss.26, 27, 32 (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968). The engine has no deduction-cap mechanism.

obligations.description: File Form IR21 for a non-Singapore-Citizen employee who ceases employment in Singapore, is posted overseas or leaves Singapore for more than three months (use the IRAS tax clearance calculator for the exceptions), withhold all monies due from the date the employer knows of it, and release or pay over on the Clearance Directive.
obligations.trigger: Notice of cessation, overseas posting or departure of a non-Citizen employee
obligations.timing: At least one month before the cessation, posting or departure; monies withheld from the day the employer is aware; tax under a Directive to Pay Tax paid within 10 days; the final salary not delayed more than 30 days after notice to the Comptroller (EA s.24(2)). Late or no filing: fine up to $5,000.
obligations.owner: Finance / IR21 submission, withheld balance and clearance directive
obligations.authority: Income Tax Act 1947 s.68(7); Employment Act 1968 s.24 (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968); IRAS, Getting tax clearance: a step-by-step guide (https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/employers/tax-clearance-for-foreign-spr-employees-(ir21)/getting-tax-clearance-a-step-by-step-guide). The engine raises a disbursement hold for a non-Citizen leaver (`payroll.tax_clearance`); filing and the release are outside it.

obligations.description: Prepare Form IR8A with Appendix 8A (benefits in kind), Appendix 8B (share gains) and Form IR8S (excess or refunded CPF) for every employee for the year; submit electronically under the Auto-Inclusion Scheme where the employer has 5 or more employees in the year, received a notice to file electronically, or is registered for AIS; otherwise give the forms to the employee.
obligations.trigger: Employment income paid in a calendar year
obligations.timing: By 1 March of the following year.
obligations.owner: Finance / AIS acknowledgement or forms given to employees
obligations.authority: Income Tax Act 1947 s.68(2); IRAS, Auto Inclusion Scheme (AIS) for Employment Income (https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/employers/auto-inclusion-scheme-(ais)-for-employment-income).

obligations.description: Maintain work injury compensation insurance for every employee doing manual work and every non-manual employee earning $2,600 or less a month.
obligations.trigger: Employing a covered employee
obligations.timing: In force for the whole period of employment.
obligations.owner: HR / insurance policy
obligations.authority: Work Injury Compensation Act 2019; MOM, Work injury compensation insurance (https://www.mom.gov.sg/workplace-safety-and-health/work-injury-compensation/work-injury-compensation-insurance).

obligations.description: Keep a Part 4 employee within 12 hours of work a day and 72 overtime hours a month unless the Commissioner exempts (and display any exemption order); allow one rest day a week and, where the employer fixes it, publish the rest-day roster before the month begins.
obligations.trigger: Scheduling or approving work for a Part 4 employee
obligations.timing: Before the month (rest-day roster, s.36(4)); continuously (s.38(5), s.38(8)); an exemption order under s.41A displayed while it applies.
obligations.owner: Operations / rosters, time records and any exemption order
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1968 ss.36, 38(5), 38(8), 41A (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968). The engine warns when the month's overtime or a day's hours pass the version's limits; rosters and exemptions are outside it.

obligations.description: Hold a due inquiry before dismissing for misconduct; unused annual leave is paid at the gross rate on any other dismissal and forfeited only on dismissal for misconduct.
obligations.trigger: Dismissal alleged to justify forfeiture
obligations.timing: Before the dismissal (s.14); the leave pay with the final salary.
obligations.owner: HR / inquiry finding and applicable statutory basis
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1968 s.14 and s.88A(8) (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968); MOM, Termination with notice (https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/termination-of-employment/termination-with-notice).

obligations.description: Notify MOM of every retrenchment; assess retrenchment benefit (no statutory entitlement under 2 years of continuous service; above it the amount is by contract or collective agreement, with the Tripartite Advisory norm of two weeks to one month of salary per year of service).
obligations.trigger: An employer registered in Singapore with at least 10 employees notifies any employee of retrenchment
obligations.timing: Within 5 working days after the affected employees are notified.
obligations.owner: HR / MOM notification acknowledgement and retrenchment package record
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1968 s.45 and s.96A (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968); MOM, Mandatory retrenchment notifications (https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/retrenchment/mandatory-retrenchment-notifications); Tripartite Advisory on Managing Excess Manpower and Responsible Retrenchment.

obligations.description: Pay the employee the government-paid maternity, paternity, shared parental, adoption and childcare leave the employer grants, then claim the reimbursable part from the Government; pay an employee away on National Service and claim make-up pay; release the employee for NS.
obligations.trigger: Government-paid leave taken, or an NS call-up
obligations.timing: GPML and GPPL claims within 3 months after the last day of the leave; GPCL and extended childcare leave within 3 months after the end of the 12-month period; later claims only with MSF approval. NS make-up pay per the MINDEF/MHA claim rules.
obligations.owner: HR / claim submissions and reimbursement receipts
obligations.authority: Child Development Co-Savings Act 2001; Enlistment Act 1970; Government-Paid Leave portal (https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/); MSF, When is the submission deadline for GPL claims (https://ask.gov.sg/msf/questions/cls1lenm302b1jzsgpnu9hn08).

obligations.description: Do not retire an employee below the minimum retirement age; offer re-employment to an eligible Singapore Citizen or SPR employee (satisfactory performance, medically fit, at least two years' service if hired at 55 or older) up to the re-employment age, or pay the Employment Assistance Payment.
obligations.trigger: An eligible employee approaches the minimum retirement age
obligations.timing: Minimum retirement age 63, re-employment up to 68 (64 and 69 from 1 July 2026). Discuss at least six months before the employee reaches the retirement age and offer the re-employment contract no later than three months before it; otherwise pay the Employment Assistance Payment.
obligations.owner: HR / re-employment offer or EAP record
obligations.authority: Retirement and Re-employment Act 1993; MOM, Re-employment (https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/re-employment).

obligations.description: Collect, use and disclose employee and applicant personal data only with consent (actual, deemed, or deemed by notification) or under a statutory exception, only for purposes a reasonable person would consider appropriate, and notify the purposes; for managing or terminating the employment relationship, inform the employee of that purpose even where consent is not required.
obligations.trigger: Collection, use or disclosure of an applicant's or employee's personal data (onboarding, payroll, CPF/IRAS filing, benefits, termination)
obligations.timing: On or before collection, use or disclosure; a new purpose needs fresh notification and consent unless an exception applies
obligations.owner: HR / privacy notice in the offer letter or employment contract
obligations.authority: Personal Data Protection Act 2012 ss.13 (consent required), 14, 15 and 15A (deemed consent), 16 (withdrawal), 17 and First and Second Schedules (without consent), 18 (limitation of purpose), 20 including s.20(4) (employment relationship) (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/PDPA2012); PDPC Advisory Guidelines on the PDPA for Selected Topics, Employment chapter (https://www.pdpc.gov.sg/-/media/files/pdpc/pdf-files/advisory-guidelines/ag-on-selected-topics/advisory-guidelines-on-the-pdpa-for-selected-topics-(revised-may-2024).pdf)

obligations.description: Give an employee access to their personal data and how it has been used or disclosed in the past year, correct errors on request, and make reasonable effort to keep data used for decisions (pay, CPF, tax) accurate and complete.
obligations.trigger: An access or correction request, or any use of personal data to make a decision affecting the employee
obligations.timing: As soon as reasonably possible (access, s.21(1)) or practicable (correction, s.22(2)); an organisation unable to respond within 30 days after receiving the request must within that time inform the applicant in writing of the time by which it will respond (Personal Data Protection Regulations 2021 reg.5)
obligations.owner: HR / request log

facts.label: Public holiday compensation
facts.description: TIME_OFF: the employer gives a day off in substitution for a public holiday on a non-working day (EA s.88(1)(c)) and time off in lieu of the extra day’s salary for public-holiday work by an employee outside Part 4 who is not a workman (s.88(4A)); PAY or empty pays them. The time owed is not banked by payroll. Default PAY: s.88(1)(c) leaves the employer to “either pay the employee for that holiday at his or her gross rate of pay or give the employee a day off in substitution”, and s.88(4A) time off “may be given … in lieu of” the s.88(4) extra day’s salary — paying discharges both, so an unrecorded election is paid (Employment Act 1968 s.88, SSO 2026-09-23).

work_rules.authority: Employment Act 1968 Part 4. s.38(4) — work beyond normal hours is paid at not less than one and a half times the hourly basic rate of pay (in this form since 1 March 1996, Act 36 of 1995). s.38(1) not more than 44 hours in one week, carried by the `weekly_normal` limit payroll reads: normal-day hours past the 44th in a Monday-to-Sunday week are overtime of the day they fall on. s.38(5) 72 overtime hours a month; s.38(8) 12 hours in any one day. s.38(1)(a) a break after more than 6 consecutive hours; s.38(1)(c) at least 45 minutes in the aggregate where work requiring continual attendance runs 8 consecutive hours. s.36 one rest day a week, and where a monthly roster is drawn up not more than 12 days between two rest days. s.37(3) rest-day pay at the employer's request; s.37(3)(c)(ii) pays the hours beyond the normal day "for each hour or part thereof", so the rest-day OT-1.5X band rounds its slice up to the hour. s.88 a public holiday falling on a rest day is observed on the next working day. s.35 and the First Schedule: Part 4 applies to a workman earning a basic monthly salary of not more than SGD 4,500 and to a non-workman (other than a manager or executive) earning not more than SGD 2,600. `overtime_when` applies both ceilings: `terms.statutory_work_category == "NON_MANUAL"` is the non-workman (SGD 2,600); every other category is a workman (SGD 4,500). s.88(4) an extra day's salary at the basic rate of pay for work on a public holiday. Rates: Fourth Schedule, hourly basic rate = 12 × monthly basic ÷ (52 × 44), carried by `rate_week_hours` (44 for every full-time monthly-rated employee, whatever the contract's week) over `ordinary_divisor_days`; Third Schedule item 2, basic rate for one day = 12 × monthly basic ÷ (52 × days required to work in a week), which the day-wage bands price directly from `person.terms` because one divisor cannot yield both figures for a week under 44 hours. s.38(1) normal day: 9 hours on a week of five days or fewer, else 8 (`normal_hours`; a longer shift is a normal day plus overtime). s.37(2): rest-day work at the employee’s request pays half a day up to half the normal hours and one day beyond (`requested_by`), against s.37(3)’s one and two at the employer’s. s.88(4A)/MOM: a public holiday that falls on a non-working day (neither a working day nor the rest day) is a day off in lieu or an extra day’s salary; the `PH-NON-WORKING-DAY` band prices the day’s salary on such a day read and found empty (a `work_days` row with no work), taking no hours. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): EA Third Schedule: the basic rate for a day is the daily rate for a daily-rated employee, the hourly rate × the hours of the normal day for an hourly-rated one, and 12 × monthly ÷ (52 × days a week) for a monthly-rated one (`person.terms.pay_frequency` in the day-wage bands). Applied 2026-09-19 (2): EA s.38(1)(a): work that must be carried on continuously may run eight consecutive hours with a break of at least 45 minutes for a meal — the break is owed at eight (`>= 8.0`), not only beyond it. Applied 2026-09-23 (SG audit): s.35 measures "a salary not exceeding $2,600 [$4,500] a month", so the Part 4 bands turn a daily, hourly or weekly rate into its month (daily × 52 × days a week ÷ 12; hourly × weekly hours × 52 ÷ 12; weekly × 52 ÷ 12) before comparing it; the raw rate put every daily- or hourly-rated employee inside Part 4. s.88 is Part 10 of the Employment Act and reaches no employee outside it: the two public-holiday bands exclude `NON_EA`. s.88(1)(c) pays a holiday on a non-working day at the gross rate of pay (s.2: allowances included, other than travelling, food or housing): the `PH-NON-WORKING-DAY` band prices a monthly-rated employee on `person.terms.monthly_wage` — basic plus the contract's fixed allowances, which can only exceed the s.2 gross rate where a travelling, food or housing allowance is fixed on the contract. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): the Part 4 salary test reads `person.terms.monthly_basic` (a daily, hourly or weekly rate taken to its month on the ordinary divisor, 52 × days ÷ 12), and the Third Schedule day reads `person.terms.ordinary_day` (12 × monthly ÷ (52 × days); a weekly wage is now its week over the days, not read as a month). s.2 “gross rate of pay” excludes travelling, food and housing allowances: `PH-NON-WORKING-DAY` prices `person.terms.gross_monthly`, net of the allowance codes in `gross_excluded_allowances` (the company’s own codes; none are seeded). s.88(1)(c) and s.88(4A): the entity fact `public_holiday_compensation` = TIME_OFF records the employer’s election of a day off instead of pay — the non-working-day band stops, and the extra day’s salary for holiday work stops for an employee outside Part 4 who is not a workman (non-workman above $2,600 or a manager); the Part 4 hours beyond the normal day stay paid.

encashment.day_amount: terms.fixed_allowances * 12.0 / (52.0 * terms.working_days_per_week) + (terms.pay_frequency == "DAILY" ? terms.basic_salary : terms.pay_frequency == "HOURLY" ? terms.basic_salary * terms.ordinary_hours_per_week / terms.working_days_per_week : terms.pay_frequency == "WEEKLY" ? terms.basic_salary / terms.working_days_per_week : terms.basic_salary * 12.0 / (52.0 * terms.working_days_per_week))
encashment.authority: Employment Act s.2 gross rate; MOM Monthly and daily salary; MOM Termination with notice: last drawn gross salary. Excludes overtime, bonuses, reimbursements, productivity incentives, travel, food and housing allowances. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5): WEEKLY, DAILY and HOURLY. EmA 1968 s.2: “gross rate of pay” is the money including allowances an employee is entitled to “for working for a period of time, that is, for one hour, one day, one week, one month”, less overtime, bonus/AWS, reimbursements, productivity incentives and travelling, food or housing allowances. Third Schedule item 2 (s.107A) prices a monthly-rated day at 12 × monthly gross ÷ (52 × days required a week); a daily rate is the day itself, an hourly rate is the day’s contractual normal hours (weekly hours ÷ days a week), a weekly rate is the week over the days required in it (item 2 on 12 months = 52 weeks), and a monthly contract allowance adds its item 2 day share. Piece rates (item 1: the 14 days before, over the days actually worked) have no pay frequency here.

deduction_ceiling.authority: Employment Act 1968 s.32(1): all deductions in a salary period other than under s.27(1)(a) (absence), (f) (advances, loans, overpayments) and (j) (co-operative society) may not exceed 50% of the salary payable for that period — CPF contributions (s.27(1)(h)) count; s.32(2): the last salary on termination or completion of the contract is outside the limit. Not applied: the per-instalment quarter caps of s.31(3) and (5).

final_pay_deadlines.authority: Employment Act 1968 s.23(2): an employee who resigns without the notice s.10 requires, or before it expires, is paid within 7 days; one who served it is paid on the last day (s.23(1), the default rule)

tax_clearance.authority: Income Tax Act 1947 s.68(5)-(7); IRAS tax clearance withholds all monies until the Clearance Directive. IRAS (Tax Clearance for Foreign & SPR Employees): a permanent resident who is not leaving Singapore permanently gives a Letter of Undertaking and no IR21 is filed, so a permanent resident is held only when recorded as leaving.

sources.instructions:
Sources are the primary instrument first — the statute or regulation in the national law database, the gazette, or the table the authority itself publishes — one page per fact the version seals, never a news article or a commentary. A historical version lists the instruments in force on its own effective date. Where the primary host refuses the reader (sso.agc.gov.sg, officialgazette.gov.ph, peraturan.bpk.go.id, kwsp.gov.my, hrdcorp.gov.my answer 403 to Norbital-Public-Page-Reader) the authority’s own published table is listed instead, or the Wayback Machine’s dated copy of the authority’s own page or PDF (web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<url>) — never a host the reader cannot open.
sso.agc.gov.sg — Singapore Statutes Online: every Act and subsidiary legislation, HTML. /Act/EmA1968 is the Employment Act; add ?ProvIds=P14- for Part 4 (ss.35–53: rest days, hours, overtime), ?ProvIds=P19- for Part 9 (sick leave), ?ProvIds=P110- for Part 10 (public holidays); a #pr37- fragment lands on one section. /Act/CPFA1953 is the CPF Act, /Act/CDCSA2001 the Child Development Co-Savings Act.
cpf.gov.sg — CPF Board. /employer/employer-obligations/how-much-cpf-contributions-to-pay links the rate tables; the tables are PDFs under /content/dam/web/employer/employer-obligations/documents/ (CPFcontributionratesfrom1Jan2026.pdf, jan2027cpfcontributionrates.pdf; 0.2 MB, text) with Tables 1–5 by citizenship year and age. /employer/infohub/news/cpf-related-announcements/new-contribution-rates announces a step. /employer/employer-obligations/skills-development-levy is SDL; /employer/employer-obligations/contributions-to-self-help-groups the CDAC/ECF/MBMF/SINDA tables.
mom.gov.sg — /employment-practices/hours-of-work-overtime-and-rest-days (44 h, 1.5×, 72 h, $4,500/$2,600), /employment-practices/public-holidays (the gazetted list per year), /employment-practices/leave/<scheme>, /employment-practices/salary/monthly-and-daily-salary.
profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg — /schemes/<maternity-leave|paternity-leave|shared-parental-leave|childcare-leave|unpaid-infant-care-leave|adoption-leave>: the entitlement, its commencement date and eligibility.
muis.gov.sg — the MBMF contribution table by wage tier.

Finding changes (read these before comparing, every run):
1) Read https://sso.agc.gov.sg/What's-New/New-Legislation/RSS (newest first). Flag titles containing Central Provident Fund, Employment, Retirement, Child Development Co-Savings, Skills Development Levy, Holidays, Income Tax (rates/reliefs/Bills), Foreign Manpower (Levy), Workplace Fairness; open the linked SL-Supp/Acts-Supp page and read the commencement clause. 2) For a sealed Act, read https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/<CODE>?ViewType=Rss — any provision with a ValidDate after the version's seal date is a candidate. A provision as at a date: /Act/<CODE>?ValidDate=YYYYMMDD&ProvIds=Sc1- (CPF First Schedule). Title search: /Search/Content?Phrase=<words>&In=InForce_Act_SL&Within=title. 3) CPF: cpf-related-announcements and news-releases pages, then the rate page and its PDF tables. 4) MOM: press-releases?category=Employment+practices (&page=N); public-holidays page carries next year's list. 5) IRAS newsroom. SSO answers 403 to non-browser UAs — use the real browser. Discovery only: https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/singapore/individual/significant-developments — then open the official instrument before citing.

exit_facts.label: Resigned with due notice
exit_facts.description: The employee resigned after giving the notice s.10 requires (or paid salary in lieu under s.11); the total salary is then due on the day the contract ends (Employment Act 1968 s.23(1)), not within 7 days (s.23(2)).

exit_facts.label: Leaving Singapore permanently
exit_facts.description: A Singapore permanent resident leaving Singapore permanently: the employer seeks tax clearance (Form IR21) and withholds all monies (Income Tax Act 1947 s.68(7)). A permanent resident who is staying gives a Letter of Undertaking instead, and no IR21 is filed.

exit_facts.label: Dismissed for misconduct
exit_facts.description: Dismissed on grounds of misconduct after due inquiry (Employment Act 1968 s.14(1)); s.88A(8) then withholds the pay for untaken annual leave.

obligations.description: Submit and pay the month's CPF contributions (employer and employee shares) for every Singapore Citizen and SPR employee, with the SDL and self-help-group deductions, through the employer's CPF Submission Number; apply to CPF Board for a refund of contributions paid in excess of the Additional Wage ceiling (the payslip never credits it back).
obligations.trigger: Wages payable for a calendar month to a Citizen or SPR employee
obligations.timing: By the 14th of the following month (the next working day if the 14th is a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday); late payment interest 1.5% a month from the day after the due date, minimum $5.
obligations.owner: Finance / CPF submission advice and payment receipt
obligations.authority: Central Provident Fund Act 1953; CPF Board, When is the due date for CPF contributions (https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/when-is-the-due-date-for-cpf-contributions) and How does CPF Board calculate interest on late payment (https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/how-does-cpf-board-calculate-interest-on-late-payment).

obligations.description: Pay the Skills Development Levy for every employee working in Singapore, foreign employees included; the per-employee levies are summed and the total rounded down to the nearest dollar. An employer with only foreign employees pays SWDA directly.
obligations.trigger: Remuneration payable for a calendar month to any employee
obligations.timing: With the month's CPF contributions, by the 14th of the following month.
obligations.owner: Finance / CPF submission advice (SDL line) or SWDA receipt
obligations.authority: Skills Development Levy Act 1979; CPF Board, Skills Development Levy (https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/skills-development-levy). The engine prices each employee's levy; the whole-dollar rounding of the total and the payment are outside it.

obligations.description: Deduct the self-help-group contribution (CDAC, ECF, MBMF, SINDA) from the wages of each employee the fund reaches and remit it with CPF; apply a fund's written opt-out or changed-amount instruction from its effective date and keep it.
obligations.trigger: Wages payable for a calendar month to an employee within a fund
obligations.timing: With the month's CPF contributions, by the 14th of the following month.
obligations.owner: Payroll / fund instruction on file and CPF submission advice
obligations.authority: CPF Board, Contributions to self-help groups (https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/contributions-to-self-help-groups). The engine prices the deduction and reads the recorded instruction; obtaining the instruction and remitting are outside it.

obligations.description: Pay the monthly foreign worker levy for every Work Permit and S Pass holder; the payroll engine does not price it.
obligations.trigger: A Work Permit or S Pass is in force during the month
obligations.timing: By the 17th of the following month (the next working day if it falls on a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday), normally by GIRO; a late payment penalty accrues, and missing two consecutive months revokes the employer's existing Work Permits and S Passes the following month.
obligations.owner: Finance / MOM levy statement and GIRO receipt
obligations.authority: Employment of Foreign Manpower Act 1990 and the levy order made under it; MOM, Paying the foreign worker levy (https://www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/work-permit-for-foreign-worker/foreign-worker-levy/paying-the-levy).

obligations.description: Employ a foreign employee only while a valid work pass is in force and cancel the pass when the employment ends; count a local employee towards the Work Permit / S Pass quota only when paid at least the Local Qualifying Salary ($1,800 a month full-time; $10.50 an hour part-time under 35 hours a week).
obligations.trigger: Hiring, pass renewal or cessation of a foreign employee; each quota computation
obligations.timing: Before the foreign employee starts work; cancellation when the employment ends; the LQS on every month counted for quota.
obligations.owner: HR / work-pass records and quota computation
obligations.authority: Employment of Foreign Manpower Act 1990 s.5(1); MOM, Local Qualifying Salary (https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/progressive-wage-model/local-qualifying-salary).

obligations.description: Give each employee a written record of the key employment terms (salary, salary period, hours, leave, deductions, and the other prescribed terms).
obligations.trigger: An employee who entered a contract on or after 1 April 2016 and is employed for 14 days or more
obligations.timing: Not later than 14 days after the day the employee starts employment.
obligations.owner: HR / issued KET record
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1968 s.95A(2) (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968).

obligations.description: Give an itemised pay slip with the prescribed items (basic salary, allowances, overtime hours and pay, other additional payments, deductions including CPF, net salary, dates) for all salary paid for each salary period, and for every sum paid on dismissal or resignation.
obligations.trigger: Every salary payment, and every payment under EA s.22 or s.23
obligations.timing: Together with the payment, or within 3 working days after it.
obligations.owner: Payroll / issued pay slips (hard copy or electronic)
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1968 s.96 (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968); MOM, Itemised pay slips (https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/salary/itemised-payslips). The engine produces the payslip content; issuing it is outside it.

obligations.description: Keep complete and accurate employee records (particulars, start and leaving dates, working hours, public holidays and leave taken) and salary records (basic salary, allowances, additional payments, deductions, overtime hours and pay, net salary, payment dates), accessible to the employee or former employee.
obligations.trigger: Every employee and former employee covered by the Employment Act
obligations.timing: Current employees: the latest two years; former employees: the last two years, kept for one year after the employee leaves.
obligations.owner: HR and Payroll / record store
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1968 s.95 (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968); MOM, Employment records (https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/employment-records).

obligations.description: Fix a salary period of not more than one month and pay salary for it on time; pay overtime separately if needed.
obligations.trigger: The close of each salary period
obligations.timing: Salary before the expiry of the 7th day after the last day of the salary period; additional payments for overtime not later than 14 days after the last day of the salary period in which the work was done.
obligations.owner: Payroll / payment records
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1968 ss.20, 21(1)–(2) (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968).

obligations.description: Pay the total salary and every sum due on termination.
obligations.trigger: Employment ends
obligations.timing: Contract completed or employee terminates with due notice or under s.11: on the last day (s.21(3), s.23(1)); dismissal: on the day of dismissal or, if not possible, within 3 days thereafter, not being a rest day or public holiday (s.22); employee leaves without notice or before notice expires: before the expiry of the 7th day after termination (s.23(2)). Subject to income-tax clearance under s.24.
obligations.owner: Payroll / payment receipt and termination record
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1968 ss.21(3), 22, 23 (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968). The engine warns when a run's pay date passes the version's `payroll.final_pay_deadlines`; those rows cannot yet tell a resignation or retrenchment with notice served (due on the last day) from one without.

obligations.description: Make only deductions the Act authorises (absence, damage or loss, consented accommodation or amenities, advances and overpayments, CPF, court or Comptroller orders, consented others) and keep the total of those subject to the limit within 50% of the salary for the period; a written consent may be withdrawn before the deduction.
obligations.trigger: Any deduction from salary
obligations.timing: Each salary period; the 50% limit does not apply to the last salary on termination.
obligations.owner: Payroll / deduction authorities and consents
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1968 ss.26, 27, 32 (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968). The engine has no deduction-cap mechanism.

obligations.description: File Form IR21 for a non-Singapore-Citizen employee who ceases employment in Singapore, is posted overseas or leaves Singapore for more than three months (use the IRAS tax clearance calculator for the exceptions), withhold all monies due from the date the employer knows of it, and release or pay over on the Clearance Directive.
obligations.trigger: Notice of cessation, overseas posting or departure of a non-Citizen employee
obligations.timing: At least one month before the cessation, posting or departure; monies withheld from the day the employer is aware; tax under a Directive to Pay Tax paid within 10 days; the final salary not delayed more than 30 days after notice to the Comptroller (EA s.24(2)). Late or no filing: fine up to $5,000.
obligations.owner: Finance / IR21 submission, withheld balance and clearance directive
obligations.authority: Income Tax Act 1947 s.68(7); Employment Act 1968 s.24 (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968); IRAS, Getting tax clearance: a step-by-step guide (https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/employers/tax-clearance-for-foreign-spr-employees-(ir21)/getting-tax-clearance-a-step-by-step-guide). The engine raises a disbursement hold for a non-Citizen leaver (`payroll.tax_clearance`); filing and the release are outside it.

obligations.description: Prepare Form IR8A with Appendix 8A (benefits in kind), Appendix 8B (share gains) and Form IR8S (excess or refunded CPF) for every employee for the year; submit electronically under the Auto-Inclusion Scheme where the employer has 5 or more employees in the year, received a notice to file electronically, or is registered for AIS; otherwise give the forms to the employee.
obligations.trigger: Employment income paid in a calendar year
obligations.timing: By 1 March of the following year.
obligations.owner: Finance / AIS acknowledgement or forms given to employees
obligations.authority: Income Tax Act 1947 s.68(2); IRAS, Auto Inclusion Scheme (AIS) for Employment Income (https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/employers/auto-inclusion-scheme-(ais)-for-employment-income).

obligations.description: Maintain work injury compensation insurance for every employee doing manual work and every non-manual employee earning $2,600 or less a month.
obligations.trigger: Employing a covered employee
obligations.timing: In force for the whole period of employment.
obligations.owner: HR / insurance policy
obligations.authority: Work Injury Compensation Act 2019; MOM, Work injury compensation insurance (https://www.mom.gov.sg/workplace-safety-and-health/work-injury-compensation/work-injury-compensation-insurance).

obligations.description: Keep a Part 4 employee within 12 hours of work a day and 72 overtime hours a month unless the Commissioner exempts (and display any exemption order); allow one rest day a week and, where the employer fixes it, publish the rest-day roster before the month begins.
obligations.trigger: Scheduling or approving work for a Part 4 employee
obligations.timing: Before the month (rest-day roster, s.36(4)); continuously (s.38(5), s.38(8)); an exemption order under s.41A displayed while it applies.
obligations.owner: Operations / rosters, time records and any exemption order
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1968 ss.36, 38(5), 38(8), 41A (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968). The engine warns when the month's overtime or a day's hours pass the version's limits; rosters and exemptions are outside it.

obligations.description: Hold a due inquiry before dismissing for misconduct; unused annual leave is paid at the gross rate on any other dismissal and forfeited only on dismissal for misconduct.
obligations.trigger: Dismissal alleged to justify forfeiture
obligations.timing: Before the dismissal (s.14); the leave pay with the final salary.

obligations.authority: Employment Act 1968 s.14 and s.88A(8) (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968); MOM, Termination with notice (https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/termination-of-employment/termination-with-notice).

obligations.description: Do not retire an employee below the minimum retirement age; offer re-employment to an eligible Singapore Citizen or SPR employee (satisfactory performance, medically fit, at least two years' service if hired at 55 or older) up to the re-employment age, or pay the Employment Assistance Payment.

obligations.authority: Retirement and Re-employment Act 1993; MOM, Re-employment (https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/re-employment).

obligations.description: Collect, use and disclose employee and applicant personal data only with consent (actual, deemed, or deemed by notification) or under a statutory exception, only for purposes a reasonable person would consider appropriate, and notify the purposes; for managing or terminating the employment relationship, inform the employee of that purpose even where consent is not required.
obligations.trigger: Collection, use or disclosure of an applicant's or employee's personal data (onboarding, payroll, CPF/IRAS filing, benefits, termination)
obligations.timing: On or before collection, use or disclosure; a new purpose needs fresh notification and consent unless an exception applies
obligations.owner: HR / privacy notice in the offer letter or employment contract
obligations.authority: Personal Data Protection Act 2012 ss.13 (consent required), 14, 15 and 15A (deemed consent), 16 (withdrawal), 17 and First and Second Schedules (without consent), 18 (limitation of purpose), 20 including s.20(4) (employment relationship) (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/PDPA2012); PDPC Advisory Guidelines on the PDPA for Selected Topics, Employment chapter (https://www.pdpc.gov.sg/-/media/files/pdpc/pdf-files/advisory-guidelines/ag-on-selected-topics/advisory-guidelines-on-the-pdpa-for-selected-topics-(revised-may-2024).pdf)

obligations.description: Give an employee access to their personal data and how it has been used or disclosed in the past year, correct errors on request, and make reasonable effort to keep data used for decisions (pay, CPF, tax) accurate and complete.
obligations.trigger: An access or correction request, or any use of personal data to make a decision affecting the employee
obligations.timing: As soon as reasonably possible (access, s.21(1)) or practicable (correction, s.22(2)); an organisation unable to respond within 30 days after receiving the request must within that time inform the applicant in writing of the time by which it will respond (Personal Data Protection Regulations 2021 reg.5)
obligations.owner: HR / request log
obligations.authority: Personal Data Protection Act 2012 ss.21, 22, 22A, 23 (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/PDPA2012); Personal Data Protection Regulations 2021 regs.4–5 (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/SL/PDPA2012-S63-2021?ProvIds=pr4-,pr5-, read 2026-09-23)

obligations.description: Protect personal data in the organisation's possession or control (payroll files, NRIC/FIN, bank accounts, medical certificates) with reasonable security arrangements against unauthorised access, collection, use, disclosure, copying, modification, disposal and loss of storage media.
obligations.trigger: Holding employee personal data, including in a payroll system or a data intermediary
obligations.timing: Continuous
obligations.owner: HR / IT security; data-intermediary contract with the payroll vendor
obligations.authority: Personal Data Protection Act 2012 s.24 (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/PDPA2012)

obligations.description: Cease to retain documents containing personal data, or anonymise them, once the purpose is no longer served and retention is no longer needed for legal or business purposes (subject to the separate statutory retention periods for employment records, CPF and tax).
obligations.trigger: End of employment, a rejected application, or expiry of the record's legal retention period
obligations.timing: As soon as it is reasonable to assume that retention no longer serves the purpose
obligations.owner: HR / retention schedule and disposal record
obligations.authority: Personal Data Protection Act 2012 s.25 (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/PDPA2012)

obligations.description: On credible grounds that a data breach occurred, assess whether it is notifiable (likely to cause significant harm, or affects 500 or more individuals); if notifiable, notify the PDPC and, where there is significant harm, the affected individuals; a data intermediary must notify the organisation without undue delay.
obligations.trigger: Credible grounds to believe a data breach affecting personal data in the organisation's possession or control has occurred
obligations.timing: Assess reasonably and expeditiously (PDPC: within 30 calendar days); notify the PDPC as soon as practicable and no later than 3 calendar days after determining the breach is notifiable; notify affected individuals as soon as practicable, at the same time as or after the PDPC
obligations.owner: DPO / breach assessment record and PDPC notification
obligations.authority: Personal Data Protection Act 2012 Part 6A ss.26A–26E, including s.26B (notifiable breaches), s.26C (duty to assess), s.26D (duty to notify) (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/PDPA2012); Personal Data Protection (Notification of Data Breaches) Regulations 2021 (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/SL/PDPA2012-S64-2021); PDPC Guide on Managing and Notifying Data Breaches (https://www.pdpc.gov.sg/-/media/files/pdpc/pdf-files/other-guides/guide-on-managing-and-notifying-data-breaches-under-the-pdpa-15-mar-2021.pdf)

obligations.description: Designate one or more individuals (the data protection officer) responsible for PDPA compliance and make the business contact information of at least one of them publicly available; develop and implement data protection policies and a complaints process and communicate them to staff.

obligations.timing: Continuous; keep the DPO contact current
obligations.owner: Management / DPO appointment record
obligations.authority: Personal Data Protection Act 2012 ss.11(3)–(5), 12 (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/PDPA2012)

facts.label: Public holiday compensation
facts.description: TIME_OFF: the employer gives a day off in substitution for a public holiday on a non-working day (EA s.88(1)(c)) and time off in lieu of the extra day’s salary for public-holiday work by an employee outside Part 4 who is not a workman (s.88(4A)); PAY or empty pays them. The time owed is not banked by payroll. Default PAY: s.88(1)(c) leaves the employer to “either pay the employee for that holiday at his or her gross rate of pay or give the employee a day off in substitution”, and s.88(4A) time off “may be given … in lieu of” the s.88(4) extra day’s salary — paying discharges both, so an unrecorded election is paid (Employment Act 1968 s.88, SSO 2026-09-23).
